headline: Record fundraising quarter powers earnings growth
summary_short: Brookfield Asset Management posted record Q2 2026 fundraising of $77 billion, driving fee-related earnings up 20% y/y to $808 million and distributable earnings up 15% y/y to $707 million ($0.44/share), while net income more than doubled q/q to $1,172 million.
summary_long: Fee-related earnings grew 20% y/y to $808M and fee-bearing capital rose 19% y/y to $672B, driven by record $77B of quarterly fundraising (private equity, infrastructure, credit) and $21B of deployment. Distributable earnings were $707M ($0.44/share), up 15% y/y. Net income of $1,172M nearly doubled q/q, aided by a $553M carried-interest income swing (from -$63M a year ago) and $199M of equity-method income. Cash rose to $1,503M from $1,045M q/q; long-term debt rose to $4,084M after issuing $1.0B of senior notes. BAM repurchased $200M of shares and declared a $0.5025/share quarterly dividend. No numeric forward guidance was issued; management cited its 'best year ever' outlook qualitatively.

drivers.explanation: CEO Connor Teskey attributed the quarter to record fundraising of $77 billion led by private equity, infrastructure, and credit, with fee-related earnings up 20% and fee-bearing capital up 19% y/y to $672 billion.

The release attributes the quarter's strong results to record capital inflows and strong deployment; the statement of operations shows a $616M carried-interest income swing (to $553M from -$63M) as the largest single revenue-line mover.

Net income growth is arithmetically explained by the same carried-interest swing plus higher base management and advisory fees ($919M vs $815M y/y) outpacing a smaller rise in compensation and operating expense.
not explained separately from the net income and revenue drivers above in the release
FRE and DE growth are explicitly tied by the company to fee-bearing capital reaching $672 billion, up 19% y/y, on $163 billion of trailing-twelve-month fundraising.
The release discloses issuance of $1.0 billion of senior notes during the quarter as a source of cash, alongside record fundraising inflows.
Debt rose after BAM issued $1.0 billion of senior notes: $550 million of five-year notes at 4.832% and $450 million of ten-year notes at 5.298%.
Equity growth is consistent with the quarter's $904 million of net income attributable to BAM being retained; the release discloses no equity issuance or major charge against equity this quarter.
